title: Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans: Terms on Which Coverage Is Given Up
content:
**Clauses in force.**

**1. Counting the full-refund window.** On a plan of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans the full-refund window is counted in whole calendar days from the day the plan was bought, that day counting as day zero, weekends and store holidays included, and part days are never rounded up.

**2. Whose act the cancellation is.** The cancellation itself is confirmed by the customer on the protection service request record, because ending coverage they paid for is theirs alone to do.

## Evidence for clause 1

The day the plan was bought is read from the plan record, and the plan the cancellation concerns is tied to that record by its own reference. The comparison is taken before the cancellation is acted on, and a cancellation reaching the desk on the last day of the window falls within it.

## Boundary readings of the window

Take coverage whose full-refund window is 45 calendar days (a hypothetical input). A cancellation reaching the desk on the forty-fifth day, counting the day of purchase as day zero, falls within the window; one reaching the desk on the forty-sixth day falls outside it. A weekend or a store holiday inside those days changes neither reading.

## Clauses no longer in force

The four clauses below are **no longer in force** and are superseded by the current basis. They are kept here so that withdrawn law is not applied; the full-refund windows, the administration fees and whether a plan prorates remain as the schedules for these plans publish them.

> A plan cancelled inside the coverage's full-refund window is refunded in whole, and the cancellation takes effect on the day the customer confirms it.

> A merchandise protection plan is refunded in whole only when the cancellation reaches the desk within the full-refund window in calendar days, counted from the date the plan was bought.

> A plan that has already settled a claim is not refunded at all, whatever window it is cancelled in, because the coverage has already answered.

> After that window the coverage that prorates returns the premium in proportion to the months of the term not yet run, less the coverage's administration fee, and the coverage that does not prorate returns nothing.
